Data: Hello Rafsan, I wanted to share a very important issue about Halal food, as I faced this exact same issue when I first started living abroad. Just because a dish is chicken or beef doesn't automatically mean it's Halal. If eating Halal is important to you, it's always best to ask the restaurant if their meat is Halal-sourced or not. Another thing to watch out for is cross-contamination. Sometimes restaurants use the same pans to cook pork, so I always make sure to ask whether they use the same pan for pork and chicken or not. After all, if we want to eat Halal, we definitely want to avoid even pork fat, even if we aren't eating the meat itself! I also always check ingredients for packaged food. I ate chocolates with haram gelatines several times. But after I realise and after doing some research I check everything carefully now. I hope this helps!! Please take this as friendly advice from a well-wisher. I’ve been watching your videos since 2017, and I just wanted to share this information in case you weren't aware! Thanks

Data: 7:45 Well Hania Amir has been asking Rafsan whether he is lefty or righty. Rafsan has been serving the Rashgullah to Hania Amir with his left hand because Rafsan's right hand is not clean i.e. his right hand is messy with food what he has been eating. If you analyse this little deeper, Bangladeshi people when they are eating their food, they do not touch water glass, serving spoon, water jug, curry dishes, boneplates etc. with their right hands they will use their left hands but out of the respectful gesture they will synchronisely utilise the right hand too but the actual action is carried by the left hand. The reason behind this is very simple, in our childhood our parents teach us not touch anything with our right hand because you are eating with it and it is the messy one. Whatever you touch with the messy hand those things will be messy too. Most importantly if you are touching things with the messy hand i.e. the right hand you will pick up germs from those items which possibly touched by others and you would not want to continue eating with that hand which picked germs by touching things. So simple solution we use right hand solely for eating and left hand for serving food, drinking water and so on so forth. Moreover we donot use tissues paper or serviette to clean our right hand because plenty lints will be in the hand after cleaning and we cannot continue eating with linty hand. Hence we totally avoid touching anything while eating with our right hand. So Rafsan was not rude by serving Rashgulla with his left hand he was just simply following the norms. In Pakistan I noticed differently as you mostly eat roti which is dry item and hand doesn’t get messy so it is easier to use the right hand to touch the water glass or serving spoon and etc. items. Jazak Allah khair
